corollaries.statement:
theorem rup_addition_preserves_equivalence {F : Formula} {C : Clause} (h : RUP F C) :
    Equivalent (C :: F) F
corollaries.plain: If RUP F C, then C :: F and F have the same models.

hypotheses.name: h : RUP F C
hypotheses.purpose: As for the main theorem.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x1, C = x0 (a one-clause formula)

corollaries.statement:
theorem equivalent_cons_iff_entails (F : Formula) (C : Clause) :
    Equivalent (C :: F) F ↔ Entails F C
corollaries.plain: For every F and C (universally quantified, no hypotheses): C :: F and F have the same models if and only if F entails C. The equivalence corollary above is therefore a restatement of the main theorem.

plain_claim: If unit propagation over F, started from the trail that assumes every literal of the clause C false, reaches a conflict within some finite budget (RUP F C), then every total assignment that satisfies F satisfies C (Entails F C). Secondary theorems: under the same hypothesis, C :: F and F have the same models (rup_addition_preserves_equivalence); and, for every F and C with no hypothesis, C :: F and F have the same models if and only if F entails C (equivalent_cons_iff_entails).

hypotheses.name: h : RUP F C
hypotheses.purpose: The propagation conflict being certified; a conflict is a complementary pair on the trail or a clause of F with all literals falsified.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x0 or x1 (one binary clause), C = x0

nonvacuity_witness: F = x0 and (not x0 or x1), C = x1: C is RUP with respect to F.
non_claims: Does not claim the converse: entailment does not imply RUP, because unit propagation is incomplete (entails_not_implies_rup), and this is not limited to unsatisfiable formulas or the empty clause (entails_not_implies_rup_satisfiable_nonempty).

Adding C preserves logical equivalence if and only if F entails C (equivalent_cons_iff_entails), for every F and C. RUP is sufficient but not necessary: the clause x0 is RAT but not RUP with respect to the satisfiable formula x0OrFullSquare, and adding it preserves equivalence because it is entailed (rat_not_rup_addition_preserves_equivalence). RAT additions in general need not preserve equivalence (rat_addition_not_equivalence).
Equivalence is over total assignments of all variables.

The theorem is about the unbudgeted predicate RUP. A passing rupCheck at any budget implies RUP (rupCheck_sound); a failing rupCheck at one budget does not by itself refute RUP, since RUP quantifies over all budgets (no separate theorem; not proved here).

Toy model: literals are (variable, polarity) pairs, clauses and formulas are lists, unit propagation is a round-based propagator with a budget. The result is a statement about this toy model; it neither establishes nor refutes the corresponding claims about production solvers and checkers (drat-trim, cake_lpr, Lean's bv_decide LRAT checker, SMT solvers that emit clausal proofs); any correspondence with them is a derived (modeling bridge) claim, not a theorem.

theorem entails_not_implies_rup_satisfiable_nonempty :
    Satisfiable x0OrFullSquare ∧ Entails x0OrFullSquare [Lit.p 0] ∧
      ¬ RUP x0OrFullSquare [Lit.p 0]

plain_claim: If p is a literal of C, C is RAT on p with respect to F (for every clause D of F containing the complement of p, the clause C followed by the literals of D other than that complement is RUP with respect to F), and a satisfies F, then ratWitness a C p -- a itself if a satisfies C, otherwise a with p made true -- satisfies C and F together.

hypotheses.name: hp : p ∈ C
hypotheses.purpose: If p is not a literal of C, flipping p need not satisfy C. RATOn itself does not include p ∈ C.
hypotheses.witness_class: F empty, C = x1, p = x0

hypotheses.name: hrat : RATOn F C p
hypotheses.purpose: Keeps the clauses containing the complement of p satisfied after the flip.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = not x0, C = x0, p = x0

hypotheses.name: ha : Satisfies a F
hypotheses.purpose: The witness is built from a model of F.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x1, C = x0, p = x0, a = all-false

nonvacuity_witness: F = (not x0 or x1), C = (x0 or not x1), p = x0, a = (x0 false, x1 true); a falsifies C, so the flip branch is exercised.
non_claims: Does not say a itself satisfies C and F; the witness can differ from a in the variable of p (as in ratOn_witness_nonvacuous, where a falsifies C).
The pivot here is any literal of C; the DRAT check fixes the first literal (rat-check-depends-on-pivot-order).

RAT additions need not preserve the models of F restricted to the variables of F: in rat_addition_loses_projected_model the pivot variable x0 occurs in F = (not x0 or x1), and no model of the extended formula agrees with the model x0 = false, x1 = true of F on x0 and x1.

ratWitness maps a model forward across one clause addition (from F to C and F). Reconstructing a model of F from a model of a formula from which RAT-checked clauses were deleted is covered here only as satisfiability (replayRatDel_sat_backward) and for one step (replayRatDel_final_model_not_original); iterated reconstruction is not proved here.

theorem ratOn_preserves_satisfiability {F : Formula} {C : Clause} {p : Lit}
    (hp : p ∈ C) (hrat : RATOn F C p) (hF : Satisfiable F) : Satisfiable (C :: F)

theorem rat_addition_equisatisfiable {F : Formula} {C : Clause} (hrat : RAT F C) :

hypotheses.purpose: Without it the formulas need not be equisatisfiable.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = not x0, C = x0

hypotheses.name: hrat : RAT F C
hypotheses.purpose: Without it an added clause can make a satisfiable formula unsatisfiable.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = not x0, C = x0

hypotheses.name: hF : Satisfiable F
hypotheses.purpose: The conclusion is about satisfiability being carried forward.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x0 and not x0, C = x1

corollaries.statement:
theorem rat_addition_loses_projected_model :
    RAT [[Lit.n 0, Lit.p 1]] [Lit.p 0, Lit.n 1] ∧
      Satisfies (fun v => v == 1) [[Lit.n 0, Lit.p 1]] ∧
      ∀ b : Assignment, b 0 = false → b 1 = true →
        ¬ Satisfies b [[Lit.p 0, Lit.n 1], [Lit.n 0, Lit.p 1]]
corollaries.plain: The blocked clause x0 or not x1 is RAT on x0 with respect to F = (not x0 or x1), F has the model x0 = false, x1 = true, and no model of (x0 or not x1) and F agrees with it on x0 and x1.

plain_claim: The clause x0 is RAT with respect to the formula x1 (no clause contains not x0), yet the model x1 = true, x0 = false of x1 is not a model of x0 and x1; so RAT addition does not in general preserve equivalence, and a RAT clause need not be entailed. Secondary theorem: the clause x0 or not x1 is RAT on x0 with respect to F = (not x0 or x1), F has the model x0 = false, x1 = true, and no model of (x0 or not x1) and F agrees with it on x0 and x1 (rat_addition_loses_projected_model).
nonvacuity_witness: The instance itself.
non_claims: Does not show any satisfiability loss: the formula stays satisfiable (rat-addition-preserves-satisfiability).

Here the added variable x0 does not occur in F. That does not mean RAT additions preserve models restricted to the variables of F: when the pivot variable occurs in F they can remove such models (rat_addition_loses_projected_model).

corollaries.statement: theorem rup_implies_ratOn {F : Formula} {C : Clause} (p : Lit) (h : RUP F C) : RATOn F C p
corollaries.plain: For every literal p: if RUP F C, then RATOn F C p. It has no nonemptiness hypothesis and holds for p not in C and for C = [], because RATOn omits the literature requirement that p be a literal of C.

hypotheses.name: h : RUP F C
hypotheses.purpose: As in the main theorem.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = not x0, C = x0, p = x0

plain_claim: If C is nonempty and RUP with respect to F, then C is RAT on its first literal with respect to F.

hypotheses.name: hne : C ≠ []
hypotheses.purpose: RAT requires a pivot: RAT F [] is False by definition, while the empty clause can be RUP. Tight (on F = x0 and not x0, C = []). The corollary rup_implies_ratOn has no such hypothesis.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x0 and not x0, C = []

hypotheses.name: h : RUP F C
hypotheses.purpose: Tight (on F = not x0, C = x0): a nonempty clause need not be RAT.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = not x0, C = x0

nonvacuity_witness: F = x0 and (not x0 or x1), C = x1.
non_claims: RAT does not imply RUP: x0 is RAT but not RUP with respect to x0OrFullSquare (rat_not_rup_addition_preserves_equivalence); x0 is RAT with respect to x1 without being entailed by it (rat_addition_not_equivalence); and x0 or not x1 is RAT with respect to not x0 or x1 (RAT_example_pos) without being entailed by it (RAT_example_pos_not_entailed).

The auxiliary predicate RATOn F C p omits the literature requirement p ∈ C, so RATOn [] [] x0 holds vacuously. Unlike RAT F C, RATOn F C p alone need not preserve satisfiability (ratOn_without_mem_unsound, ratOn_sat_tight_mem); together with p ∈ C it does (ratOn_preserves_satisfiability). The corollary rup_implies_ratOn should be read with that in mind: it says nothing about satisfiability for p ∉ C.
Stated for the unbudgeted predicates RUP and RAT; the analogous statement for the budgeted checkers rupCheck and ratCheck at a fixed budget is not stated (not proved here).

corollaries.statement:
theorem lrat_hint_replay_implies_entails {F : Formula} {C : Clause} {hints : List Nat}
    (h : lratRupCheck F C hints = true) : Entails F C
corollaries.plain: If lratRupCheck F C hints = true, then F entails C.

hypotheses.name: h : lratRupCheck F C hints = true
hypotheses.purpose: As in the main theorem.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x0 or x1, C = x0, hints = [0]

plain_claim: If replaying the hinted clauses of F in order from the negation of C succeeds -- each hinted clause has exactly one non-falsified literal occurrence, which is pushed on the trail (it may already be there), until a hinted clause has no non-falsified literal occurrence, after which remaining hints are not examined -- then budgeted propagation from the negation of C reaches a conflict within (number of hints) rounds, so C is RUP with respect to F and F entails C.

hypotheses.name: h : lratRupCheck F C hints = true
hypotheses.purpose: The hint replay succeeds.
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x0 or x1, C = x0, hints = [0]

nonvacuity_witness: chain3 = x0, (not x0 or x1), not x1 with hints [0, 1, 2] for the empty clause.

Hint replay is order-sensitive: permuting an accepted hint list can make it rejected (lrat-hint-order-matters). This is not the same as incompleteness, which is treated in lrat-hint-replay-complete-wellformed.

corollaries.statement:
theorem lratRupCheckDedup_exists_iff_rup (F : Formula) (C : Clause) :
    (∃ hints, lratRupCheckDedup F C hints = true) ↔ RUP F C
corollaries.plain: For every F and C: some hint list is accepted by lratRupCheckDedup F C if and only if RUP F C, where lratRupCheckDedup first tests the negated clause for a complementary pair and replays hints on deduplicated literals. No hypotheses; the main theorem follows because lratRupCheckDedup and lratRupCheck agree on well-formed inputs (lratRupCheckDedup_eq_of_wellformed).

corollaries.statement:
theorem lratRupCheck_rejects_blocked_resolvent :
    RUP [[Lit.n 0, Lit.p 1]] (resolventOn [Lit.p 0, Lit.n 1] [Lit.n 0, Lit.p 1] (Lit.p 0)) ∧
      ∀ hints, lratRupCheck [[Lit.n 0, Lit.p 1]]
        (resolventOn [Lit.p 0, Lit.n 1] [Lit.n 0, Lit.p 1] (Lit.p 0)) hints = false
corollaries.plain: The tautological resolvent x0 or not x1 or x1 of the blocked clause x0 or not x1 (pivot x0) with not x0 or x1 is RUP with respect to not x0 or x1, and lratRupCheck rejects every hint list for it.

tier_note: LRAT is designed so that hints can be produced for RUP steps of well-formed clauses; the precise toy statement, with both side conditions shown tight (each on the witness class recorded in its ledger entry; they are not logically necessary, see lratRupCheck_side_conditions_not_necessary), is not known to be mechanized elsewhere. Not claimed novel.
plain_claim: If C contains no complementary pair of literals (NonTautological C), no clause of F repeats a literal (DupFreeClauses F), and C is RUP with respect to F, then some hint list is accepted by lratRupCheck F C. Each side condition is tight: dropping either one admits an instance in which C is RUP and every hint list is rejected (lratRupCheck_incomplete_tautology, lratRupCheck_incomplete_dup_lits). hypotheses.purpose: Accepted hint lists certify RUP (lrat_hint_replay_implies_rup).
hypotheses.witness_class: F = x0 or x1, C = x0
